correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary forest, subsets of j edges impose j independent equalities in Stam's K-box allocation, giving exactly Bin(e,1/K) conditional law; graph cycles violate the exponent. The ratio k^n/k! has decreasing log-successive ratio with derivative -(n/x+1)/(x+1). Its mode lies O(1) from n/W(n), and summing ratios yields an explicit O(n exp(-c sqrt n)) tail outside n^(3/4)/W(n). This tail is o(W(n)/n), so good-event Taylor expansion proves uniform relative zero-violation probability even at e=n-1. Le Cam coupling proves uniform moving Poisson total variation and independence provides the fixed-r product. Pure-standard-library checker passed 75 exhaustive forest histograms and one cycle boundary; finite checks do not substitute for analytic proof.

value.rationale: The motivating finite-model expansion problem has a natural FO compatibility sentence between a fixed forest predicate and independent equivalence relations. Its probability can vanish as W(n)/n, so a CLT or absolute-probability o(1) estimate is scientifically uninformative. The theorem determines the correct relative first-order probability, uniformly for every labelled forest including maximal spanning trees, plus a complete moving-Poisson collision profile and a sharp acyclicity boundary for conditional independence. This is a motivated structural and quantitative classification, not an arbitrary small-instance census.
